claims.text: NiFeCoCr-based rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys can exhibit a magnetic transition near room temperature or another refrigeration operating window.
Partial short-range chemical ordering in NiFeCoCr-based alloys creates magnetoelastic coupling.
The magnetoelastic coupling produced by partial short-range order amplifies the magnetocaloric response at fields of at most approximately 1–2 T.
Partial short-range ordering preserves rapid magnetic-domain-wall motion and consequently low hysteresis.
The ordered alloy retains a sufficiently ductile matrix for mechanical stability.
Systematically varied isothermal annealing times and temperatures can induce different degrees of short-range order in the alloy.
The degree of short-range order is correlated with local lattice strain.
The degree of short-range order is correlated with an evolving magnetic-domain structure.
Partial chemical ordering produces local lattice distortions that couple to the magnetic transition.
Coupling between local lattice distortions and the magnetic transition enhances the magnetic entropy change.
Partial chemical ordering improves domain-wall mobility.
Excessive ordering reduces domain-wall mobility or magnetoelastic coupling, thereby degrading the magnetocaloric effect or increasing hysteresis.
A fully random chemical arrangement can reduce domain-wall mobility or magnetoelastic coupling.
Samples with intermediate short-range order will have larger low-field isothermal entropy changes than samples with minimal or excessive order.
Samples with intermediate short-range order will have lower hysteresis than samples with minimal or excessive order.
Samples at the proposed optimal ordering level will retain mechanical integrity during thermomagnetic cycling.
The beneficial effect should persist through moderate annealing temperatures up to approximately 300–400 °C provided long-range order and second-phase precipitation are avoided.
Complete disorder or fully developed long-range order diminishes low-field magnetocaloric performance.
A conventionally quenched NiFeCoCr-based alloy with minimal short-range order has weaker low-field magnetocaloric performance or greater hysteresis than a suitably annealed alloy.
